jobs.title: Full Stack Developer
jobs.description: Develop end-to-end solutions using Python, React, Typescript, and AI integrations.

fullDescription.overview: As a Full Stack Developer at Robles.AI, you will build scalable, high-performance web applications that integrate AI-powered services. You'll collaborate with data scientists, AI engineers, and designers to deliver intuitive, impactful products.
responsibilities: Design, develop, and maintain full stack applications using React, Typescript, and Python.
Integrate REST APIs, GraphQL endpoints, and AI model outputs into the frontend.
Implement responsive user interfaces and ensure cross-device compatibility.
Collaborate with AI teams to integrate machine learning models into production systems.
Optimize application performance, scalability, and security.
Participate in code reviews, architecture discussions, and agile sprint planning.
requirements: 3+ years of experience as a Full Stack Developer.
Proficiency in Python, React, and Typescript.
Familiarity with RESTful APIs, GraphQL, and microservices architectures.
Experience deploying applications with Docker or cloud-native platforms.
Basic understanding of AI/ML concepts (bonus for OpenAI or Hugging Face experience).
Excellent problem-solving and teamwork skills.

jobs.title: Machine Learning Engineer
jobs.description: Design, train, and deploy Deep Learning models, specializing in neural network architectures.

fullDescription.overview: As a Machine Learning Engineer, you will develop and deploy advanced Deep Learning models to solve complex challenges across computer vision, NLP, and predictive analytics. You'll work alongside our AI research and product teams to deliver production-ready models.
responsibilities: Design and implement deep learning architectures for various applications.
Train, validate, and fine-tune models using PyTorch and TensorFlow.
Develop robust data pipelines for model training and evaluation.
Monitor and optimize model performance in production.
Document experiments, research findings, and best practices.
Collaborate with software engineers to integrate models into production systems.
requirements: 2+ years of experience in Machine Learning or Deep Learning.
Strong understanding of neural network architectures (CNNs, RNNs, Transformers).
Hands-on experience with PyTorch or TensorFlow.
Experience with large datasets, data augmentation, and preprocessing techniques.
Knowledge of MLOps is a plus (model serving, retraining loops).
Strong foundation in linear algebra, probability, and optimization.

jobs.title: Generative AI Engineer
jobs.description: Build and optimize RAG (Retrieval Augmented Generation) pipelines and prompt engineering workflows.

fullDescription.overview: As a Generative AI Engineer, you will design, build, and optimize applications powered by large language models (LLMs). You'll specialize in Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) systems, prompt engineering, and integrating generative AI into real-world workflows.
responsibilities: Develop RAG architectures combining LLMs with vector databases (Pinecone, FAISS).
Design and optimize prompts to enhance model outputs (prompt engineering).
Integrate OpenAI APIs, Hugging Face models, or self-hosted LLMs.
Implement conversation memory and dynamic chaining using LangChain or similar frameworks.
Evaluate, test, and improve generative model responses.
Document prompt libraries, pipelines, and optimization strategies.
requirements: 2+ years working with LLMs, NLP models, or Generative AI systems.
Hands-on experience with OpenAI, Hugging Face, LangChain, or similar.
Strong understanding of RAG concepts and vector search.
Familiarity with Pinecone, Weaviate, or Chroma.
Creative thinking and strong experimentation skills.
Experience with fine-tuning and evaluation metrics for generative models is a plus.

jobs.title: Computer Vision Engineer
jobs.description: Create intelligent vision systems using OpenCV, TensorFlow, and edge deployment strategies.

fullDescription.overview: As a Computer Vision Engineer, you will develop AI-powered visual recognition systems across industries. You'll design and deploy solutions for object detection, tracking, segmentation, and video analysis.
responsibilities: Design and train computer vision models for classification, detection, and segmentation.
Implement traditional vision algorithms using OpenCV (feature extraction, tracking, OCR, etc.).
Deploy vision models to cloud and edge devices (NVIDIA Jetson, Coral, mobile).
Optimize models for real-time inference and edge deployment.
Collaborate with software teams to integrate vision pipelines into broader applications.
Write clean, scalable, and well-documented vision system code.
requirements: 2+ years of experience in Computer Vision or related fields.
Proficiency with OpenCV, TensorFlow, or PyTorch.
Experience with model optimization (TensorRT, ONNX, pruning, quantization).
Knowledge of video analytics, motion tracking, and real-time processing.
Familiarity with edge deployment and hardware acceleration (GPU, TPU).
Strong analytical skills and attention to detail.

try-identity.title: Identity Verification API
try-identity.description: See our facial biometric matching in action. Upload a selfie and a photo ID, and the API detects the face in each, compares them, and returns a match score in seconds.
try-identity.instructions: Your images are processed only for this demo and are not stored permanently. Upload a clear, well-lit selfie and a photo ID where the face is fully visible for the best results.
try-identity.webhook_hint: Results are also posted to this endpoint when processing finishes. This is a sample URL for the demo.
try-identity.selfie_hint: A clear photo of your face, looking at the camera.
try-identity.document_hint: Passport, ID card or driver's license with a visible photo.
try-identity.dropzone_cta: Click to upload or drag a file
try-identity.log_empty: Run a verification to see the API requests and responses here.
try-identity.log_call_warming: Waking up the service before sending your images…
try-identity.log_call_sending: Sending both images to the API…
try-identity.log_call_polling: Checking the result every 3 s until it's ready.
try-identity.status_pending_description: The request has been received and is waiting to be processed.
try-identity.status_failed_description: The verification failed due to an error (e.g., unreadable image or no face detected).
try-identity.status_partially_completed_description: Images were compared successfully, but some data is still being uploaded.
try-identity.status_completed_with_errors_description: The process finished, but some images or steps failed during upload or analysis.
try-identity.status_completed_description: The request was processed successfully and all data was uploaded.
try-identity.results_distance_hint: Cosine similarity between the two face embeddings. Higher means more alike.
try-identity.results_images_hint: Detected faces and 3D facial landmarks extracted by the model.
try-identity.service_ready: Service ready — you can run verifications instantly.
try-identity.service_cold_hint: This demo runs on on-demand infrastructure that sleeps when idle. The first verification may take ~30s while resources spin up; after that, runs are instant. It will warm up automatically when you start.
try-identity.service_warming: Preparing the service… this can take up to ~30s the first time. Please wait — the verification will start automatically once resources are ready.
try-identity.service_warm_failed: The service is taking longer than expected to start. Please try again in a moment.
try-identity.tip_upload: Upload two images: a selfie and a photo ID. They are sent to the API, which detects and compares the faces.
try-identity.tip_webhook: When processing finishes, the API also POSTs the result to this callback URL. Here it's a sample endpoint for the demo.
try-identity.tip_results: Summary returned by the API after comparing the two faces, including the match decision and similarity score.
try-identity.tip_match: Whether the API considers both faces to belong to the same person, based on the similarity threshold.
try-identity.tip_distance: Cosine similarity between the two 512-dimensional face embeddings. Ranges 0–100%; higher means more alike.
try-identity.tip_images: Images returned by the model: the detected face crops and the 3D facial landmarks it extracted from each input.
try-identity.tip_log: Raw HTTP requests and responses exchanged with the API in real time, so you can see exactly what the demo sends and receives.
try-identity.tech_subtitle: Technical definition, flow and model details
try-identity.tech_flow_1: The browser uploads both images to storage and sends their URLs to POST /recognition/verify-id, which creates a request (status: pending).
try-identity.tech_flow_2: A processing step (POST /cron/verify-id) downloads the images and runs the face model.
try-identity.tech_flow_3: The model detects a face in each image, extracts an embedding, and compares them.
try-identity.tech_flow_4: The client polls GET /recognition/get/{id} every 3s until the status is completed, and the result is also POSTed to the callback.
try-identity.tech_model_note: The model is pretrained and runs on CPU (inference only — no training happens). It outputs a 512-dimensional embedding per face.
try-identity.tech_api_1: REST API over HTTPS with JSON payloads; processing is asynchronous with a webhook callback.
try-identity.tech_api_2: Image URLs are validated server-side (allow-listed hosts) before fetching.
try-identity.tech_api_3: Demo images are processed for the verification only and are not intended for long-term storage.
try-identity.how_step1_desc: A selfie and a photo ID, converted to base64 right in your browser.
try-identity.how_step2_desc: It detects each face, extracts an embedding and computes similarity.
try-identity.how_step3_desc: A score and match decision in seconds, plus a webhook callback.
try-identity.results_ready: Your images are ready — run the verification.
try-identity.results_locked: Upload a selfie and a photo ID to run a verification.
try-identity.samples_cta: No photos handy? Use sample images
try-identity.samples_hint: A fictional demo pair — same face on both, so the match actually works.

try-object.title: Object Detection
try-object.description: Detect and label objects in real time — from your webcam or an uploaded image. The model runs entirely in your browser.
try-object.model_loading: This happens once — your browser caches it for next time.
try-object.model_error: Couldn't load the model. Check your connection and reload the page.
try-object.how_title: From your camera to labeled results, in seconds
try-object.how_step1_desc: Your live camera or an uploaded image.
try-object.how_step2_desc: TensorFlow.js detects objects locally, in your browser.
try-object.how_step3_desc: Boxes, classes and confidence scores, instantly.
try-object.camera_empty_title: Detect objects live from your camera
try-object.camera_empty_desc: Point it at everyday things — people, laptops, cups, phones — and watch them get labeled in real time.
try-object.camera_permission_hint: Your browser will ask for permission. The video never leaves your device.
try-object.camera_error: Access was blocked or no camera was found. Allow it in your browser and try again, or analyze an image instead.
try-object.upload_hint: JPG, PNG or WebP · processed locally, never uploaded
try-object.threshold_tip: Hides detections scored below this value. Lower it to see more — and noisier — guesses.
try-object.detections_empty: Start the camera or analyze an image — every object the model finds is listed here.
try-object.detections_none: No objects above the confidence threshold. Lower it or try another scene.
try-object.log_live_desc: Detecting objects locally, frame by frame…
try-object.log_empty: Capture a frame from the camera or analyze an image to see the raw model output here.
try-object.tech_flow_1: Capture: a frame is read from your webcam (or the uploaded image) — nothing leaves the device.
try-object.tech_flow_2: Inference: TensorFlow.js runs the COCO-SSD model on your device's GPU (WebGL) to locate objects.
try-object.tech_flow_3: Output: for each object the model returns a bounding box, a class label and a confidence score.
try-object.tech_flow_4: Render: boxes and labels are drawn on a canvas over the video, refreshed every frame in real time.
try-object.tech_note: COCO-SSD is a single-shot detector trained on the COCO dataset (80 everyday object classes). Running it in-browser means zero server cost, no cold starts and full privacy.

try-emotion.title: Emotion Recognition
try-emotion.description: Detect faces and read facial expressions in real time — 7 emotions, from your webcam or an uploaded photo. Runs entirely in your browser.
try-emotion.privacy: 100% private: face detection and expression analysis run locally in your browser. No images or biometric data are ever uploaded or stored.
try-emotion.model_loading: Loading the face models… this happens once and is then cached by your browser.
try-emotion.model_ready: Models ready — start the camera or upload a photo.
try-emotion.model_error: Couldn't load the models. Check your connection and reload the page.
try-emotion.tip_mode: Use your live camera to read expressions in real time, or upload a photo to analyze it once.
try-emotion.tip_run: The model detects each face, plots a 68-point landmark mesh and scores 7 facial expressions.
try-emotion.camera_error: Couldn't access the camera. Please grant permission, or use the upload option instead.
try-emotion.camera_placeholder: Press "Start camera" to begin real-time analysis.
try-emotion.upload_cta: Click to choose a photo, or drag one here
try-emotion.upload_hint: The photo is processed locally — nothing is uploaded
try-emotion.tip_expressions: Probability the face is showing each emotion right now. They sum to ~100%.
try-emotion.log_subtitle: The raw model output for each analyzed frame or photo
try-emotion.log_empty: Start the camera and log a frame, or upload a photo, to see the model output here.
try-emotion.tech_flow_1: Detect: a lightweight face detector (Tiny Face Detector) finds every face in the frame.
try-emotion.tech_flow_2: Landmarks: a second model plots 68 facial points (eyes, brows, nose, mouth) per face.
try-emotion.tech_flow_3: Classify: an expression network scores 7 emotions from the aligned face.
try-emotion.tech_flow_4: Render: the box, landmark mesh and top emotion are drawn over the video every frame.
try-emotion.tech_note: Powered by face-api.js on TensorFlow.js. All inference happens on your device's GPU — no server, no cold starts, and no biometric data ever leaves your browser.

try-langchain.title: LangChain Agent
try-langchain.description: Chat over your own documents (RAG), let an agent use tools, or extract structured JSON — all powered by LangChain.

try-langchain.upload_hint: PDF, TXT or DOCX — used only for this session

try-langchain.request_error: The request failed. The service may be waking up — try again.
try-langchain.network_error: Couldn't reach the service. It may be waking up (cold start) or offline — try again in a moment.
try-langchain.placeholder_rag: Ask a question about your uploaded documents…
try-langchain.placeholder_tools: Ask the agent to compute or look something up…
try-langchain.placeholder_json: Describe what you want summarized as structured JSON…
try-langchain.service_cold_hint: The API scales to zero when idle. Your first request will warm it up (may take ~30s).
try-langchain.service_warm_failed: The service is taking longer than usual to wake up. Please try again in a moment.
try-langchain.how_step1_desc: RAG, an agent with tools, or structured JSON output.
try-langchain.how_step2_desc: Type a question, or add documents first for RAG.
try-langchain.how_step3_desc: See the exact API call and JSON response on the right.
try-langchain.mode_rag_desc: Answers grounded only in the documents you add.
try-langchain.mode_tools_desc: Reasons step by step and calls tools to get it done.
try-langchain.mode_json_desc: Turns a request into clean, structured data.

try-langchain.kb_preview_hint: Read-only preview · this is the text the model searches

try-langchain.tech_endpoint_upload: Receives the files (multipart) and stores them temporarily.
try-langchain.tech_endpoint_ingest: Splits, embeds and indexes them in your session's vector store.

try-langchain.tech_endpoint_json: Structured output: summary, bullets and citations.
try-langchain.log_subtitle: Live requests to the LangChain API and their JSON responses.
try-langchain.log_empty: Send a message and the API calls will appear here with their JSON responses.
try-langchain.tip_session: Each session isolates your uploaded documents and chat history. Start a new one to reset everything.
try-langchain.tip_mode: RAG answers from your uploaded docs; Agent uses tools to reason and act; JSON returns a structured summary.
try-langchain.tip_mode_rag: Retrieval-Augmented Generation: the agent answers using the documents you ingest in this session.
try-langchain.tip_mode_tools: A LangChain agent that can call tools (e.g. calculator, search) to reason step by step.
try-langchain.tip_mode_json: Returns a structured JSON object (summary, bullets, citations) instead of free text.
try-langchain.tip_upload: Files are ingested into a vector store scoped to your session, then used to answer RAG questions.
try-langchain.tip_ask: Your input is sent to the LangChain API; watch the exact request and JSON response on the right.
try-langchain.tip_answer: The parsed answer from the API response. The full raw JSON is shown in the activity log.
try-langchain.tech_subtitle: The pipeline and stack behind this demo
try-langchain.tech_flow_1: You pick a mode and (for RAG) upload documents that get embedded into a vector store.

try-rag.title: Ask your documents
try-rag.description: Upload a PDF and ask it questions: a full RAG pipeline indexes it, finds the relevant passages, reranks them for precision and answers with two LLMs, citing the sources.
try-rag.dropzone_idle: Drop a PDF here or click to choose one
try-rag.dropzone_hint: Read locally in your browser — the file is never sent
try-rag.dropzone_sample_hint: A fictional company's travel & remote-work policy
try-rag.hash_error: Could not read the PDF text in your browser. Try a different PDF or browser.
try-rag.no_text: No selectable text was found in this PDF. It may be a scanned document (images only), which this demo can't process — try a PDF with real text.
try-rag.process_error: The document text could not be processed. The service may be busy — please try again in a moment.
try-rag.tip_step1: The text is extracted from your PDF right here in your browser — the file itself is never sent. A SHA-256 hash of that text becomes the Pinecone namespace, so the same document isn't indexed twice; the backend re-hashes the text to verify.
try-rag.extracted_label: View extracted text (what is sent to the API)
try-rag.tip_step2: Each chunk is turned into a vector embedding (a numeric representation of its meaning) and stored in the Pinecone vector database under this document's namespace.
try-rag.tip_step3: Your question is embedded and compared to every chunk by cosine similarity. We fetch the top 65 — a deliberately wide net: vector search is fast but approximate, so we over-retrieve candidates here and let the slower, more accurate reranker (step 4) narrow them down. Too few now would risk dropping the truly relevant passage.
try-rag.tip_step4: Two-stage reranking on those 65 candidates. First MonoT5 (a T5 model) labels each chunk relevant/not-relevant to filter out noise cheaply. Then BGE, a cross-encoder, reads the question and each surviving chunk together and scores them — far more accurate than the initial vector similarity, but too costly to run on the whole database, which is why it only runs on the pre-filtered top candidates.
try-rag.tip_step5: The top reranked chunks are given to two LLMs (Llama and GPT-4) as context so they answer grounded in your document instead of hallucinating.
try-rag.service_cold_hint: This demo runs on on-demand infrastructure that sleeps when idle. The first step may take ~30s while resources spin up; after that, it's fast. It warms up automatically when you start.
try-rag.service_warming: Preparing the service… this can take up to ~30s the first time. Please wait — it will start automatically once resources are ready.
try-rag.service_warm_failed: The service is taking longer than expected to start. Please try again in a moment.
try-rag.tech_flow_1: Ingest: the PDF text is extracted in the browser (pdf.js) and the API splits it into overlapping chunks; a SHA-256 hash of the text becomes the Pinecone namespace.
try-rag.tech_flow_2: Embed & index: chunks are embedded with sentence-transformers and upserted (in batches) into the Pinecone vector index.
try-rag.tech_flow_3: Retrieve: the question is embedded and the top-K most similar chunks are fetched by cosine similarity.
try-rag.tech_flow_4: Rerank: a MonoT5 → BGE cross-encoder re-scores candidates for precision.
try-rag.tech_flow_5: Generate: the top chunks are passed as context to Llama and GPT-4 to produce grounded answers.
try-rag.tech_note: A RAG pipeline lets an LLM answer using your own documents, reducing hallucinations by grounding responses in retrieved source text.

try-rag.how_simple_privacy: Your PDF never leaves your browser: only the extracted text is sent, and the same document is never indexed twice.
try-rag.tech_privacy_1: The PDF is processed in the browser with pdf.js; only the extracted text reaches the API.
try-rag.tech_privacy_2: The namespace is a SHA-256 hash of the text: the same document isn't re-indexed, and the backend verifies the hash.
try-rag.tech_privacy_3: No OCR: scanned PDFs without a text layer produce no text.

try-rag.step_extract_desc: The PDF is read in your browser
try-rag.step_index_desc: It's stored in the vector database
try-rag.step_generate_desc: GPT-4 and Llama write the answer

try-rag.runner_waiting_question: Document ready · Robly is waiting for your question
try-rag.rerank_phase_2: Pairing your question with each passage so they're read together…
try-rag.rerank_phase_3: MonoT5 checks, passage by passage, whether it really answers your question…
try-rag.rerank_phase_4: Dropping the passages that only look similar but don't help…
try-rag.rerank_phase_5: BGE, a cross-encoder, reads question and passage at once and scores them…
try-rag.rerank_phase_6: Fine-tuning: this model understands context better than similarity search…
try-rag.rerank_phase_7: Sorting the passages from most to least relevant…
try-rag.rerank_phase_8: On the first query the models are still loading into memory: it can take up to ~45 s…
try-rag.rerank_loop_1: The server sleeps when nobody uses it; on wake-up it loads the models from scratch…
try-rag.rerank_loop_2: Model weights are read from disk on the first inference; after that it's much faster…
try-rag.rerank_loop_3: That's {{count}} question–passage pairs, each going through the full model…
try-rag.rerank_loop_4: This is the most expensive step, which is why it only runs on the shortlisted candidates…
try-rag.rerank_loop_5: Vector search is fast but approximate; the reranker is slow but precise…
try-rag.rerank_loop_6: Almost there: once it's done, the best passages go to GPT-4 and Llama…
try-rag.generate_phase_1: Building the context from the top {{count}} passages…
try-rag.generate_phase_2: Sending your question and the context to GPT-4 and Llama…
try-rag.generate_phase_3: GPT-4 and Llama are writing the answer…
try-rag.generate_phase_4: Waiting for both models to finish…
try-rag.generate_loop_1: The models can only use passages from your document, so they don't make things up…
try-rag.generate_loop_2: Each model answers separately so you can compare them…
try-rag.generate_loop_3: Almost there: putting together the cited sources…
